title: Research sprint goal: Census deterministic 2: fewer sources need reading
goal: The sprint goal's open questions, whose kb coverage was weak or none on 2026-10-10, are answered with the kb tools first and the live docs for the gaps, and the findings are written as kb facts and gap entries through the kb skills, so each committed item can name the knowledge it needs: (1) GitHub REST API for issues, discussions and repositories: which field dates the last change (updated_at, pushed_at), conditional requests with ETag/If-None-Match and whether a 304 counts against the unauthenticated rate limit, and that limit; (2) a github.com wiki page: its change signal (the wiki's git repository, <repo>.wiki.git, and its history); (3) a Learn page's public MicrosoftDocs source repository: how original_content_git_url maps a page to a repository path and whether that repository's git history can date the page (the kb has the meta tags, lacks the git side); (4) Python urllib: how a name-resolution or connection failure surfaces (URLError whose reason is socket.gaierror or ConnectionError, EAI_NONAME), so a retry can tell it from an HTTP error. Questions already good (the Learn meta tags, ms.date as a weak signal) stand as findings.
